model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral mixin for federated identity equivalence: recording that two endpoint identifiers are asserted to denote the same subject, with the asserting authority, mapping predicate, justification, confidence and temporal validity, and for governing how such assertions may be traversed, clustered and reported without becoming silent inferences.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 covers the assertion, qualification, traversal and derived-view semantics of alias / same-as relations between identifiers held by different systems, registries or vocabularies. It owns the alias edge (endpoints, predicate binding, strength profile, justification, authority, confidence, validity interval, retraction), the graph formed by those edges, the declared policy under which that graph may be traversed, the evidence record produced by a traversal, and the registration, lineage and integrity reporting of equivalence-cluster views and canonical-representative references that external authorities calculate. It deliberately stops at the point where a decision is executed: it does not match, merge, reason, rewrite or enforce.
in_scope: Alias edge assertion between two endpoint identifiers, with the asserting authority, mapping predicate IRI, justification reference and confidence
Classification of edge strength and the symmetry / transitivity profile that each mapping predicate licenses
Not-same (difference) assertions recorded as first-class edges alongside same-as edges
Temporal validity of an alias assertion and its retraction or supersession as an append-only record
Alias graph structure, node and edge identity, and edge-level annotation
Declared traversal policy: allowed predicate set, direction, maximum depth and path count, repeated-node rule, termination and reproducibility
Path evidence records: ordered edge list, hop count, weakest-edge strength, contradiction markers and traversal provenance
Registration of externally calculated equivalence-cluster views with their rule identifier, rule version, input digest and snapshot instant
References to externally decided canonical representatives, with selecting authority, rule version, scope and effective interval
Cluster split and merge lineage, retained aliases, historical member lookup and downstream-reference impact reporting
Integrity findings over the alias graph and registered clusters, expressed as reported results with severities
out_of_scope: Entity resolution, record linkage, similarity scoring or candidate-match generation that produces new alias edges
Execution of ontology reasoning or entailment closure; materialising owl:sameAs consequences over property assertions
Master-data merge, survivorship and golden-record construction, and the selection of a canonical representative
Mutation of endpoint identities, endpoint records or endpoint-owning systems
HTTP redirect handling, IRI dereferencing and content negotiation
Authentication, authorisation decisions and enforcement of access rules
Capture, storage and integrity of audit trails, even where audit record references are carried here
Execution of retention, disposition, destruction or erasure
Definition or governance of the endpoint identifier schemes themselves
Label, name and translation equivalence between strings rather than between identified subjects

boundary_notes.distinction: That model decides that two records probably describe the same subject and emits candidate matches. WM-XCT-036 records the resulting assertion with its justification and confidence and governs how it may be traversed; it never computes a match. SSSOM makes this explicit by requiring a mapping_justification on every mapping, which is supplied by the producing process, not by the mapping record itself.

OWL 2 SameIndividual makes the named individuals interchangeable in the interpretation, so entailment can propagate every property. Enumerating a path through alias edges is evidence, not entailment: WM-XCT-036 returns candidate paths and never writes back an inferred identity assertion. SHACL likewise permits but does not require entailment and does not modify the input graph.

Choosing which member of an equivalence cluster is the canonical representative is a preference decision owned by a master-data or curation authority. WM-XCT-036 carries the reference to that decision, its rule version, scope and effective interval, and never converts preference into equivalence or rewrites endpoint identities. Neither OWL 2 nor RDF 1.2 privileges one IRI in a set of co-denoting IRIs.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Vocabulary and thesaurus mapping model (ISO 25964-2, SKOS)
boundary_notes.distinction: Concept-scheme mapping distinguishes exact, inexact and partial equivalence between concepts and constrains how mappings may be chained. WM-XCT-036 reuses those predicates as edge classifiers and inherits their integrity conditions, but does not own concept schemes, thesaurus structure or the editorial mapping workflow.

Generic identifier and reference-binding semantics for the endpoints (what an identifier is, how it is minted, how a reference resolves) belong to the parent model. WM-XCT-036 adds only the equivalence relation between two such references and the graph and cluster semantics over it.

Traversal runs and snapshot registrations store a reference to an audit record identifier. Holding that reference does not grant ownership of audit capture, tamper-evidence, log retention or replay; those remain with the audit model.

WM-XCT-036 records retention class references and tombstones for its own edges, reports and snapshots, and can report which paths and clusters an erasure would impact. Deciding the schedule and executing destruction or erasure belongs to the retention and privacy models of the adopting Dimension.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Runtime validation engine (SHACL processor or equivalent)
boundary_notes.distinction: Integrity conditions are expressed here and their results are reported here with severities. The evaluator that runs them, and any enforcement action taken on a violation, sit outside this model; a reference to that evaluator does not transfer evaluation or enforcement semantics into WM-XCT-036.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Structural Specification and Functional-Style Syntax (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Normative source for SameIndividual (owl:sameAs) and DifferentIndividuals (owl:differentFrom) assertions, and for the absence of a unique name assumption: distinct IRIs are neither same nor different unless asserted. Grounds edge strength classes, not-same edges and the rule that traversal evidence is not entailment.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Section 10 defines the mapping properties and their formal profile: S42 exactMatch is a sub-property of closeMatch, S44 closeMatch/exactMatch/relatedMatch are symmetric, S45 exactMatch is transitive, and closeMatch is deliberately not transitive to avoid compound errors across schemes. S46 makes exactMatch disjoint with broadMatch and relatedMatch. Grounds the per-predicate transitivity profile, traversal restriction and contradiction detection.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Provides Entity/Activity/Agent, wasDerivedFrom, wasGeneratedBy, generatedAtTime, used, wasAttributedTo, qualifiedDerivation and Bundle. Grounds path provenance, cluster snapshots as derived entities, split/merge lineage as revision and derivation, and the separation of the deriving activity from the derived view.

sources.title: SPARQL 1.1 Query Language
sources.relevance: Property paths define arbitrary-length connectivity matching: it does not introduce duplicates and does not count the number of ways a connection can be made, and 'the graph matched may include cycles. Connectivity matching is defined so that matching cycles does not lead to undefined or infinite results.' Grounds repeated-node handling, duplicate-path suppression and the fact that a standard traversal operator returns solutions, not new assertions.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: Defines validation reports (sh:ValidationReport, sh:ValidationResult, sh:focusNode, sh:sourceShape, sh:resultSeverity) and the severities sh:Violation, sh:Warning and sh:Info; and states that processors MAY operate on graphs that include entailments, pre-computed or on the fly, without modifying the input graph. Grounds integrity reporting structure and the separation of validation reporting from enforcement.

sources.title: RDF 1.2 Concepts and Abstract Data Model
sources.relevance: Defines graphs as sets of triples, triple terms and reification via rdf:reifies, where a reifier identifies a triple term without asserting it, and states that two different appearances of an IRI denote the same resource. Grounds edge-level annotation, the distinction between asserted and merely referenced statements, and endpoint node identity. Not yet a Recommendation, so used as an alignment rather than a conformance target.

sources.title: A Simple Standard for Sharing Ontology Mappings (SSSOM) — Specification: Data Model
sources.version_or_date: SSSOM specification, data model page, version 1.1 documentation
sources.relevance: Defines the Mapping class with required subject_id, object_id, predicate_id and mapping_justification (there is no mapping without a justification), plus confidence, author_id, mapping_date, mapping_tool, mapping_tool_version, subject_source, object_source, predicate_modifier and similarity_score; and the MappingSet with mapping_set_id, mapping_set_version, curie_map, license and sssom_version. Grounds edge justification, confidence, predicate modifiers and mapping-set versioning as membership evidence.

sources.title: RFC 3339 — Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines the Internet date/time profile requiring seconds and either 'Z' or a numeric offset, with '-00:00' reserved for the case where the offset is unknown, semantically distinct from 'Z' or '+00:00'. Grounds the timestamp rule for snapshot instants, effective intervals and the separation of event time from observation time.

sources.title: ISO 25964 — the international standard for thesauri and interoperability with other vocabularies (data model and XML schema)
sources.organization: National Information Standards Organization (NISO), host of the freely published ISO 25964 data model and schema
sources.relevance: ISO 25964-2 covers interoperability with other vocabularies and distinguishes equivalence, hierarchical and associative mappings and exact, inexact and partial equivalence. Grounds the graded strength classification of alias edges. The normative text is paywalled; only the freely published data model and schema material was consulted, so the alignment is recorded as partial.

sources.title: When owl:sameAs Isn't the Same: An Analysis of Identity in Linked Data
sources.organization: Springer (ISWC 2010, LNCS 6496), Halpin, Hayes, McCusker, McGuinness, Thompson
sources.relevance: Argues that owl:sameAs encodes one point on a similarity scale and is often too strong for its actual uses, and that referentially opaque contexts exist in which inference should not propagate. Used as a counterexample source justifying graded edge strength, substitution licensing and the prohibition on silently materialising identity from traversal. Bibliographic metadata verified; full text behind a publisher gateway.

sources.title: The sameAs Problem: A Survey on Identity Management in the Web of Data
sources.organization: arXiv (Raad, Pernelle, Saïs, Beek, van Harmelen)
sources.relevance: Survey establishing that incorrect identity links have wide-ranging effects in a global knowledge space and that identity-link quality is an unresolved problem. Used only to justify contamination, cluster-reliability and integrity-safeguard findings as real risks, not to derive normative structure.

sources.title: OxO2 — A SSSOM mapping browser for logically sound crosswalks
sources.relevance: Documents that a prior mapping browser produced crosswalks that were not necessarily logically sound and lacked provenance, and that restricting derivation to conditions the mapping standard defines is what makes chained mappings usable. Supports the traversal-policy and predicate-composition findings as practice evidence; the specific hop limits are implementation choices, not standards.

bundles.name: Alias graph structure and governed traversal
bundles.description: The alias graph as a first-class object — its nodes, edges, per-predicate strength profile — together with the declared policy under which the graph may be walked and the evidence record a walk produces. Covers bounds, cycles, repeated nodes, path provenance, weakest-edge reporting, contradiction markers and the boundary between reporting a path and asserting an identity.
bundles.rationale: Alias assertions are only useful when chained, but chaining is exactly where the semantics break: SKOS makes exactMatch transitive while deliberately refusing transitivity to closeMatch to avoid compound errors, and OWL 2 makes SameIndividual a full interchangeability claim. A governed traversal surface is therefore required, and it must be separable from the reasoning engine that would otherwise materialise conclusions. SPARQL 1.1 supplies the only widely normative statement about how arbitrary-length connectivity is to behave with respect to duplicates and cycles.

layers.name: Graph structure and edge qualification
layers.description: What a node and an edge are in the alias graph, how each is identified and annotated, and what each mapping predicate licenses in terms of symmetry, transitivity, strength and substitution.

findings.name: Alias graph node and edge structure
findings.description: The alias graph is a directed multigraph whose nodes are endpoint identifiers held by external systems and whose edges are the alias assertions themselves. An edge carries its own identity so that it can be annotated, cited in a path, contradicted or retracted independently of its endpoints; endpoint identity remains owned by the endpoint's system of record. Nodes are not created by this model — a node exists in the graph only because at least one edge references it.

questions.text: What constitutes a node in the alias graph, and does referencing an identifier in an edge create any claim about that identifier beyond the edge itself?
answer_data: Node definition rule: a node is an endpoint identifier appearing as subject or object of at least one recorded edge
Statement that node presence carries no existence, validity or ownership claim about the referenced subject
Reference to the endpoint's system of record or governing namespace

questions.text: How is an individual alias edge identified so that it can be cited in a path, annotated or retracted without ambiguity?
answer_data: Edge identifier value and the authority that issued it
Canonical edge tuple used for digest computation (subject IRI, predicate IRI, object IRI, predicate modifier)
Digest algorithm identifier and the digest value
Rule that two edges with identical tuples but different asserting authorities are distinct edges

questions.text: Is the recorded direction of an edge semantically meaningful, or is it a storage artefact of a symmetric assertion?
answer_data: Asserted direction flag (subject-to-object as asserted)
Symmetry profile of the predicate, indicating whether the reverse direction is licensed without a second assertion
Canonical ordering rule used so that a symmetric pair yields one digest

questions.text: What annotations may be attached to an edge, and how are they kept distinct from the edge assertion itself?
answer_data: Annotation type list (justification reference, confidence, contradiction marker, integrity result, retraction)
Reification or edge-annotation binding used by the projection, recording that annotating a statement does not assert it
Annotating agent reference and annotation instant

data_elements.name: Alias edge identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a single alias assertion, stable across annotation, contradiction and retraction.

data_elements.name: Subject endpoint reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the identifier appearing in the subject position of the assertion, resolved to an absolute IRI or governed identifier.

data_elements.name: Object endpoint reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the identifier appearing in the object position of the assertion.

data_elements.name: Asserted edge direction
data_elements.description: Whether the stored orientation is the orientation as asserted, or a canonicalised orientation of a symmetric assertion.

data_elements.name: Edge annotation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an annotation about the edge that does not itself assert the edge, such as a contradiction marker or integrity result.

data_elements.name: Canonical edge digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical edge tuple, used to detect duplicates and to bind path reports to exact edge states.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Node and edge structure is the model's own reference semantics rather than a produced deliverable. Nodes are pointers into external systems of record and edges are records already governed by the alias assertion surface of this mixin; introducing a separate 'graph document' artefact here would create a second, competing statement of edge existence and invite drift between the artefact and the asserted edges. Any concrete serialisation of the graph is a projection into a storage format, which this model is explicitly independent of.

findings.name: Edge predicate strength and composition profile
findings.description: Each alias edge binds a mapping predicate whose formal profile determines whether the edge is symmetric, whether it may be chained, and whether it licenses substitution of one endpoint for the other. OWL 2 SameIndividual is a full interchangeability claim; SKOS exactMatch is transitive while closeMatch is explicitly not, precisely to prevent compound error across schemes; ISO 25964-2 distinguishes exact from inexact and partial equivalence. Not-same edges are recorded in the same structure with a modifier, so that a contradiction is visible as data rather than inferred at read time.

questions.text: Which mapping predicate does this edge bind, and from which governed vocabulary is that predicate drawn?
answer_data: Predicate IRI and source vocabulary reference (OWL 2, SKOS, or a registered local vocabulary)
Strength class assigned to the predicate (full interchangeability, exact equivalence, close or inexact equivalence, partial equivalence, related, not-same)
Predicate modifier where the edge negates the predicate

questions.text: Does this predicate permit chaining with another edge, and under what composition rule?
answer_data: Transitivity flag and symmetry flag for the predicate
Composition table stating which predicate pairs may be chained and what predicate the resulting path is reported under
Explicit prohibition on chaining non-transitive predicates such as closeMatch
Reference to the vocabulary statement that establishes the profile

questions.text: How is an explicit not-same assertion recorded so that it constrains rather than merely comments on the graph?
answer_data: Not-same edge with its own identifier, authority and justification reference
Predicate modifier or difference predicate IRI used
Scope statement declaring which contexts the difference claim applies to
Statement that the absence of an alias edge is not a difference claim, because no unique name assumption applies

questions.text: How are strength classes ordered, and is that order defined for predicates drawn from different vocabularies?
answer_data: Ordered strength lattice with each class mapped to its source vocabulary term
Cross-vocabulary comparability statement, including any pairs declared incomparable
Fallback rule when a predicate has no registered strength class

data_elements.name: Mapping predicate reference
data_elements.description: IRI of the predicate that the edge binds, drawn from a governed vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Predicate strength class
data_elements.description: Position of the predicate on the registered strength lattice, from full interchangeability down to related or not-same.

data_elements.name: Transitivity flag
data_elements.description: Whether the predicate is declared transitive by its defining vocabulary and may therefore be chained with itself.

data_elements.name: Symmetry flag
data_elements.description: Whether the predicate is declared symmetric, determining whether reverse traversal is licensed without a separate assertion.

data_elements.name: Predicate modifier
data_elements.description: Modifier that negates or qualifies the predicate, used to record not-same edges in the same structure as same-as edges.

data_elements.name: Substitution license
data_elements.description: Whether and in which contexts the edge licenses substituting one endpoint for the other, recognising that some contexts are referentially opaque.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The strength and composition profile is reference lookup data derived from external vocabularies that this model aligns to rather than owns. Publishing it as an artefact would present a local copy of OWL 2 and SKOS profile facts as though this model were their source; instead the profile is carried inline on each edge and on a registered predicate table whose authoritative statements resolve back to the defining vocabulary.

layers.name: Traversal policy and termination control
layers.description: The named, versioned policy that bounds any walk of the alias graph: which predicates may be followed, in which direction, how deep, how many paths, how cycles and repeated nodes are treated, and how a run reports why it stopped.

findings.name: Declared traversal policy, bounds and repeated-node handling
findings.description: Traversal is never ad hoc: every walk executes under a named policy version that fixes the allowed predicate set, direction, maximum hop depth, maximum returned path count and result cap, and the treatment of cycles and repeated nodes. SPARQL 1.1 establishes the baseline that arbitrary-length connectivity matching does not introduce duplicates and does not count the number of ways a connection can be made, and that cycles must not lead to undefined or infinite results; this model makes those guarantees explicit and adds finite bounds so that runs are reproducible and citable. Every run reports a termination reason, distinguishing exhaustion from bound-limited truncation.

questions.text: Who owns this traversal policy version, and what approval was required before results under it could be published?
answer_data: Policy owner reference and approving role
Approval instant and approval record reference
Statement of which decisions the policy is fit to support and which it is not

questions.text: What maximum hop depth and maximum path count apply, and what happens when a walk reaches either bound?
answer_data: Maximum depth value in hops and maximum returned path count
Truncation behaviour and whether truncated results may be cited
Rule that a truncated result is never reported as an exhaustive answer

questions.text: How are cycles and repeated nodes handled so that a walk terminates and does not report the same connection more than once?
answer_data: Repeated-node rule (simple path only, node-visit-once, or bounded revisit)
Duplicate-path suppression rule aligned with connectivity matching that does not count the number of ways a connection can be made
Cycle detection outcome recorded as a diagnostic rather than an error where the cycle is legitimate under a symmetric predicate

questions.text: In what state did the traversal terminate, and can a consumer tell truncation from exhaustion?
answer_data: Termination reason code (exhausted, depth bound reached, path cap reached, time budget reached, integrity stop)
Counts of nodes visited, edges examined and paths returned
Flag indicating whether further paths may exist beyond the bound

questions.text: What must be recorded for a traversal result to be reproducible by a different agent at a later time?
answer_data: Policy identifier and immutable version tag
Input graph digest or snapshot reference pinning the edge set walked
Ordering rule applied to returned paths
Statement of any non-deterministic element and how it is bounded

data_elements.name: Traversal policy identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the named traversal policy under which a run executes.

data_elements.name: Traversal policy version
data_elements.description: Immutable version tag of the policy; any change to bounds, predicate set or repeated-node rule produces a new version.

data_elements.name: Allowed predicate set
data_elements.description: The set of predicate IRIs the walk may follow, together with the permitted direction for each.

data_elements.name: Maximum hop depth
data_elements.description: Upper bound on the number of edges in any returned path.

data_elements.name: Maximum returned path count
data_elements.description: Upper bound on the number of distinct paths returned by a single run.

data_elements.name: Repeated-node rule
data_elements.description: Declared treatment of nodes already visited on the current path and across the run.

data_elements.name: Termination reason
data_elements.description: Why the run stopped, distinguishing exhaustion from any bound-limited truncation.

artifacts.name: Alias traversal policy profile
artifacts.description: The versioned, approved declaration of allowed predicates and directions, hop and path bounds, repeated-node and cycle rules, ordering, time budget and termination semantics, against which every traversal run is executed and every path report is bound.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Policy identifier issued by the adopting Dimension's policy register (authoritative master system for policies), combined with an immutable version tag; a digest over the canonical policy form binds published reports to the exact bounds in force. The version tag and approval instant are qualifiers, never the identifier.

layers.name: Path evidence and the inference boundary
layers.description: What a traversal produces: an ordered, provenance-bearing path record whose reported strength is that of its weakest edge, carrying contradiction markers, and explicitly typed as candidate evidence rather than an identity assertion.

findings.name: Path provenance and weakest-edge reporting
findings.description: A returned path is a derived entity: it records the ordered list of edge identifiers traversed, the hop count, the policy version and input digest under which it was produced, the agent and activity that produced it, and its production instant. Its reported strength is the strength of its weakest edge and never higher, because a chain is only as good as its least certain link; where per-edge confidence values exist they are reported alongside, not multiplied into a single reassuring number. PROV-O supplies the derivation, attribution and generation vocabulary.

questions.text: What exactly is recorded for a returned path so that a reader can re-inspect every link in it?
answer_data: Ordered list of edge identifiers with their canonical digests
Hop count and the endpoint pair
Policy identifier and version, input graph digest
References to the per-edge justifications supplied by the asserting authorities

questions.text: Which edge on this path is the weakest, and how is the path-level strength derived from it?
answer_data: Reference to the weakest edge and its strength class
Path strength class equal to the minimum edge strength on the path
Per-edge confidence values reported individually with their source
Explicit prohibition on any aggregation that reports a path stronger than its weakest edge

questions.text: At what instant was the path produced, and over which state of the graph?
answer_data: Traversal run instant in RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset
Input graph snapshot reference or digest identifying the edge state walked
Validity interval of each edge on the path at the run instant, where edges carry validity

questions.text: Which agent ran this traversal and on whose behalf, and who is accountable for citing the result?
answer_data: Traversing agent reference and, where distinct, the requesting principal reference
Audit record reference issued by the referenced audit model
Named accountable role for downstream citation of the report

data_elements.name: Path record identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a single returned path within a traversal run.

data_elements.name: Ordered edge list
data_elements.description: The sequence of edge identifiers traversed from subject endpoint to object endpoint, in order.

data_elements.name: Hop count
data_elements.description: Number of edges on the path, checked against the policy maximum depth.

data_elements.name: Weakest edge reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the edge on the path with the lowest strength class, which sets the path strength.

data_elements.name: Reported path strength
data_elements.description: Strength class of the path, equal to the minimum strength class present on it.

data_elements.name: Traversal run instant
data_elements.description: Observation time at which the traversal executed, distinct from the event times at which the traversed edges were asserted.

data_elements.name: Traversing agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent that ran the traversal, for attribution of the derived path record.

artifacts.name: Alias path evidence report
artifacts.description: The output record of one traversal run: the returned path set with ordered edge lists, per-path hop count and weakest-edge strength, contradiction markers, termination reason, policy binding, input digest and run provenance. Framed throughout as candidate evidence for a human or an external decision process.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Where the executing query or workflow system is the authoritative master system for run records, its run identifier is the report identifier; otherwise a governed IRI in the adopting Dimension's report namespace; otherwise a ULID minted here and recorded with the minting agent. The report also carries a digest over the ordered edge lists plus policy version; the run instant is a qualifier and is never the identifier.

findings.name: Non-materialisation rule and contradiction markers
findings.description: The controlling constraint of the whole traversal surface: a path is evidence of connectivity, not an assertion of identity, and running a traversal must never write a new alias edge back into the graph. OWL 2 SameIndividual is a strong interchangeability claim and DifferentIndividuals its explicit negation, with no unique name assumption making silence informative; SHACL processing likewise does not modify the graph it reads. Where a path or a cluster spans an explicit not-same edge, or joins a pair whose predicates are disjoint under SKOS S46, the result is marked with a contradiction marker that travels with it and blocks summarisation as a confirmed equivalence.

questions.text: What prevents a traversal result from being written back as a new alias edge, and how is that state visible on the record?
answer_data: Assertion status code distinguishing asserted edges from derived candidate paths
Explicit prohibition statement carried on every derived record
Name of the external process authorised to convert a candidate into an assertion, and the separate justification it must supply

questions.text: Which contradiction conditions raise a marker on a path or cluster, and what does a marker forbid downstream?
answer_data: Marker condition list (path spans an explicit not-same edge; disjoint predicates asserted between the same pair; equivalence asserted where a difference claim holds in the same scope)
References to the conflicting edges that raised the marker
Downstream prohibition: a marked result may not be reported as a confirmed equivalence and may not be used as membership evidence until resolved
Resolution state and the authority responsible for resolving it

questions.text: If entailment closure over these edges is wanted, which component owns it and what does this model hand over?
answer_data: Reference to the external reasoning or entailment service and its owning authority
Statement that computing, storing and refreshing entailments lies outside this model
The edge set, predicate profiles and policy bindings handed over as input
Statement that holding this reference confers no evaluation or execution semantics here

questions.text: What must a consuming system be told so that it does not mistake a candidate path for an established equivalence?
answer_data: Mandatory fields on every exported path record: assertion status, path strength, weakest edge, termination reason, contradiction markers
Rule that unknown or unparsed contradiction markers are treated as blocking rather than ignorable
Statement that substitution licensing is context-dependent and not implied by connectivity

data_elements.name: Assertion status
data_elements.description: Whether a record is an asserted edge from a named authority or a derived candidate produced by traversal.

data_elements.name: Contradiction marker
data_elements.description: Coded marker raised where a path or cluster conflicts with an explicit difference claim or with a disjointness condition on the bound predicates.

data_elements.name: Contradiction evidence reference
data_elements.description: References to the specific conflicting edges or assertions that caused a marker to be raised.

data_elements.name: Entailment owner reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the external reasoning or entailment service that owns closure computation, carried without transferring evaluation semantics into this model.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding is a constraint and a set of flags, not a deliverable. The non-materialisation rule has to be enforced as a field on every derived record and every export, and contradiction markers must travel inline with the path or cluster they qualify; packaging them into a separate artefact would let a consumer receive a path record without its blocking marker attached, which is the exact failure the finding exists to prevent. Where a marker needs adjudication, that adjudication record belongs to the authority that resolves it, not here.

bundles.name: Equivalence cluster boundary, representatives and lineage
bundles.description: Equivalence clusters and canonical representatives treated strictly as derived views and external decisions: how a cluster snapshot is registered with its calculation rule, version, inputs and validity; how a representative reference is carried without rewriting endpoints; how split and merge lineage preserves prior membership and prior representative decisions; and how graph pathologies are reported.
bundles.rationale: Transitive closure over identity links produces very large classes whose quality depends entirely on the weakest links inside them, and incorrect identity links have wide-ranging effects across a federated knowledge space. The cluster is therefore not a fact but a calculation output that must be pinned to a rule version and an input state to be citable at all, and the choice of a representative within a cluster is a preference decision no standard supplies — OWL 2 and RDF 1.2 both leave co-denoting IRIs equal in standing. PROV-O provides the derivation and revision vocabulary needed to keep the resulting lineage inspectable.

layers.name: Derived cluster views and external representative references
layers.description: Registration of externally calculated equivalence clusters as immutable, reproducible snapshots, and the carrying of canonical-representative decisions as references to an external authority's rule rather than as local identity changes.

findings.name: Equivalence cluster as a registered derived view
findings.description: An equivalence cluster is a view computed by an external reasoning or master-data process, not a fact this model holds. It enters the model only by registration, and only with the calculation rule identifier, the rule version, a digest of the input edge state, the snapshot instant and the membership evidence for each member. Snapshots are immutable: a corrected calculation yields a new snapshot linked as a revision of the prior one. Reproducibility is a property of the record — a snapshot that cannot be regenerated from its recorded inputs and rule version is marked unreproducible and may not be cited as membership evidence.

questions.text: Which calculation rule and rule version produced this cluster, and which authority owns that rule?
answer_data: Calculation rule reference and immutable rule version
Owning authority reference for the rule and for its change control
Parameters supplied to the rule, including the predicate set and any strength threshold applied
Statement that this model registers the output and does not execute the rule

questions.text: As of what instant does this cluster membership hold, and over what interval may it be cited?
answer_data: Snapshot instant in RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset
Registration instant recorded separately from the snapshot instant
Validity interval or expiry after which the snapshot must be recalculated before citation
Reference to the superseding snapshot once one exists

questions.text: For each member of this cluster, what evidence places it in the cluster?
answer_data: Per-member reference to the edge set or path that connects it to the cluster
Weakest edge strength on that connecting evidence
Justification references carried from the underlying assertions
Any member admitted by rule-specific criteria rather than by a recorded path, flagged as such

questions.text: What is stored so that an independent party can regenerate this exact cluster?
answer_data: Input graph digest pinning the edge state used
Rule identifier, rule version and full parameter set
Snapshot digest over the sorted member list

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form of an alias edge is the tuple of absolute subject IRI, predicate IRI, absolute object IRI and predicate modifier, with all compact identifiers expanded before hashing; the digest is taken over that form only.
For a symmetric predicate the digest orders the two endpoint IRIs lexicographically so that a symmetric pair yields a single digest, while the asserted direction is retained separately as a flag.
The canonical form of a path is the ordered list of edge identifiers plus the traversal policy identifier and version; an unordered set of edges is not a canonical path and is not citable.
The canonical form of a cluster snapshot is the lexicographically sorted member IRI list plus the calculation rule identifier, rule version, parameter set and snapshot instant.
All instants are normalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z before hashing; an offset of -00:00 records an unknown local offset and is not normalised to Z.
patch_rules: Alias edges are append-only: an edge found to be wrong is superseded by a retraction record carrying the retracting authority, reason and evidence, and the original edge is retained so that prior paths and snapshots remain interpretable.

A registered cluster snapshot is immutable; a corrected calculation produces a new snapshot linked as a revision of the superseded one, and the superseded snapshot is retained for historical membership lookup.

Any change to allowed predicates, direction, maximum depth, maximum path count or the repeated-node rule creates a new traversal policy version; previously issued path reports keep their original policy reference and are never re-bound.
Representative decisions are closed and succeeded, never overwritten: the prior decision keeps its effective interval and its authority and rule version.

Patches never rewrite endpoint identifiers or endpoint records; an endpoint change is executed by the owning master-data model and appears here only as an integrity finding and, where applicable, a snapshot annotation.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional edge annotation, a new integrity condition code or a new strength class below the existing lattice is backward compatible; removing a strength class, or changing a predicate's declared transitivity or symmetry profile, is breaking and requires a new lattice version.

Tightening a traversal bound breaks reproducibility of previously issued reports and therefore requires a new policy version identifier rather than an in-place edit; loosening a bound likewise, since path sets are not monotone under bound changes.
Consumers must treat an unknown contradiction marker or an unknown integrity severity as blocking rather than ignorable, and must not summarise a record carrying one as a confirmed equivalence.

Exported path and snapshot records must always carry assertion status, policy or rule version and weakest-edge strength; an export profile that omits any of these is not a compatible projection of this model.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the artefact — the external calculation system's snapshot identifier, the publishing authority's mapping-set identifier, the query or workflow system's run identifier, or the change-management system's report identifier.

Governed global identifier or IRI from a registered namespace, used when no master-system identifier exists — for example an SSSOM mapping_set_id IRI, a predicate IRI, or a governed IRI in the adopting Dimension's report namespace.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded together with the minting agent and the reason no upstream identifier was available.

A date, snapshot instant, rule version, policy version or content digest is a qualifier used for binding and reproducibility checks and is never used alone, or in combination with a name, as an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every instant is recorded in RFC 3339 form with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; the offset -00:00 is reserved for a genuinely unknown local offset and is not equivalent to Z or +00:00. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded as separate fields wherever they can differ: the instant at which an alias edge was asserted or retracted by its authority, at which a cluster split or merge took effect, and at which a representative decision became effective are event times; the instant at which a traversal ran, a snapshot was registered, an integrity check executed, or a record was ingested here are observation or ingestion times. Where both exist both are stored, no derived value is written into the other, and every report states which of the two it is ordered and filtered by. Durations and effective intervals are expressed as a pair of such instants, with an open end meaning still in force rather than unknown.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: An artefact marked serial carries a series key and a monotonically increasing integer within that series in two separate fields — for lineage and impact reports the series key is the cluster-line identifier and the integer is the next unused sequence number in that line. The sequence is never derived from a date or timestamp, never reset on a calendar boundary, and never reused after a withdrawal; a withdrawn number keeps its tombstone. Any concatenated form is a display label only and is not the identifier of record.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every stored artefact carries a digest over its canonical form together with the identifier and version of the policy or rule that produced it and a digest of the inputs it consumed. A cluster snapshot that cannot be regenerated from its recorded rule version, parameters and input digest is marked unreproducible and may not be cited as membership evidence; a path evidence report whose edge digests no longer match the current edge states is marked stale and must be re-run before citation, with the original retained. Digest mismatch is reported as an integrity result with a severity and never triggers an automatic correction.

policies: Traversal returns candidate paths as evidence only: producing, publishing or citing a traversal result never creates, implies or materialises an alias assertion between the endpoints, and only a separately authorised process supplying its own justification may turn a candidate into an assertion.

No cluster membership, representative reference or lineage record may exist here without a resolvable reference to the external calculation or selection rule, its immutable version and its owning authority; unattributed clusters and representatives are rejected at registration.

A path, cluster or representative record carrying an unresolved contradiction marker is always reported with that marker attached and may not be summarised as a confirmed equivalence or used as membership evidence until the owning authority resolves it.

Strength and confidence are reported at the weakest edge on the path; any aggregation that would report a path or a membership as stronger than its weakest link is prohibited, and non-transitive predicates are never composed into a chained claim.

Prior membership, prior representative decisions, superseded snapshots and retracted edges are preserved and remain queryable for their retention period, so that a historical citation can always be reconstructed rather than re-derived from current data.

read: Read candidate paths for an endpoint pair under a named traversal policy version, always returning the policy identifier and version, hop count, weakest edge, path strength, contradiction markers and termination reason together with the paths.
Read a registered cluster snapshot as of a stated instant, returning the member list, per-member evidence references, calculation rule identifier and version, input digest and reproducibility status.
Read the representative reference in force for a cluster at a stated instant and scope, returning the selecting authority, rule version and effective interval, or an explicit none-recorded result.

Read historical cluster membership and closed representative decisions from retained snapshots and lineage records; historical answers are served from what was retained and are never recomputed from the current graph.
create: Create an alias edge only with a subject endpoint, an object endpoint, a predicate IRI drawn from a registered vocabulary, an asserting authority and a justification reference; an edge without a justification is rejected, following the rule that there is no mapping without a justification.
Create a path evidence report only as the output of a traversal run bound to an approved traversal policy version and an input graph digest, with the traversing agent and run instant recorded.

Create a cluster snapshot only by registering an externally calculated result together with its rule identifier, rule version, parameter set, input digest, snapshot instant and per-member evidence; this model never creates a cluster by computing one.

Create a representative reference only with a named selecting authority, rule reference, rule version, scope descriptor and effective interval; no representative may be created by local ranking or default.
update: Updates are restricted to appends: annotations, contradiction markers, integrity results, reproducibility status, retraction records and supersession links may be added, while asserted edges, registered snapshots and issued reports remain immutable.
A changed representative decision is recorded as a new reference with its own effective interval while the prior reference is closed and retained; overwriting a prior decision is prohibited.

A changed traversal bound, allowed predicate set or repeated-node rule is issued as a new policy version; previously issued reports keep their original policy binding and are never re-bound to the new version.

No update may alter an endpoint identifier, an endpoint record or the membership of an already registered snapshot; such changes belong to the endpoint's system of record and to the external calculation owner respectively.
delete: Alias edges, path evidence reports, cluster snapshots, lineage records and representative references are not hard-deleted by default. Withdrawal is recorded as a tombstone carrying the record identifier, the withdrawal reason, the withdrawing authority, the event time at which the withdrawal took effect and the observation time at which it was recorded here, so that prior membership and prior representative decisions remain discoverable and historical citations remain reconstructable.

Retention classes and disposition schedules for these records are set by the referenced adopting-Dimension retention and disposition policy model; that model owns the schedule and executes destruction, and WM-XCT-036 stores only the retention class reference and the resulting disposition outcome reference alongside the surviving tombstone.

Erasure required by a privacy or legal authority is decided and executed by the adopting Dimension's privacy and retention models. This model's contribution is bounded: it reports which paths, snapshots, lineage records and downstream citations an erasure would impact, and afterwards records the tombstone. It neither authorises, evaluates nor performs the erasure.

Deletion of an endpoint identity is never in scope here; endpoint removal is executed by the referenced master-data model or the endpoint's system of record, and is reflected in WM-XCT-036 only as a stale-member integrity finding, an annotation on the affected immutable snapshots and, where the local edge is withdrawn, a tombstone.

A tombstone is itself retained for at least as long as the longest retention class of any record that cited the withdrawn item; where the retention model directs destruction of the tombstone, the disposition outcome reference is the last surviving trace and the loss of historical lookup capability is recorded as a known consequence.

roles.name: Alias graph steward
responsibilities: Maintain the edge register, the predicate strength lattice and the composition table, and keep each lattice entry resolvable to the vocabulary statement that establishes it
Ensure every edge carries an asserting authority and a justification reference, and reject those that do not
Record retractions and supersessions as append-only entries and preserve the originals

roles.name: Traversal policy owner
responsibilities: Author, version and obtain approval for traversal policy profiles, including allowed predicates, bounds and the repeated-node rule
Declare which decisions results under a given policy version are fit to support, and which they are not
Approve any broader policy version requested after a safeguard breach, and record the approval

roles.name: Cluster snapshot registrar
responsibilities: Register externally calculated snapshots only with a resolvable rule reference, rule version, parameter set, input digest and per-member evidence
Run and record reproducibility checks and mark unreproducible snapshots as non-citable
Record lineage events with event time and record time separately and preserve superseded snapshots

roles.name: Integrity reviewer
responsibilities: Run and interpret integrity checks over the graph and registered snapshots and assign severities from the registered condition set
Raise and track contradiction markers to resolution by the owning authority without repairing edges or membership locally
Escalate false-strong-edge, stale-member and orphaned-representative findings to the accountable external owners

roles.name: Access and disclosure custodian
responsibilities: Apply the scope-level entitlement model to edges, paths, snapshots and integrity findings and administer masking of sensitive endpoint identifiers
Record the justification reference and audit record reference for every exception and break-glass read
Maintain the retention class bindings and issue tombstones when the retention model reports a disposition outcome

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Read entitlement is evaluated per scope and granted to named roles by the adopting Dimension's access model, which owns authentication, the authorisation decision and its enforcement; WM-XCT-036 records the entitlement scope and the resulting disclosure but never evaluates or enforces a grant. Write entitlement is narrower than read: only the alias graph steward may record edges and retractions, only the cluster snapshot registrar may register snapshots and lineage, and no role may edit an issued report.
exceptions: Contradiction markers, integrity condition codes and severities remain visible to any principal already entitled to read the affected edge, path or cluster, even where the underlying evidence document is restricted, because withholding a blocking marker is more harmful than disclosing its existence.

Endpoint identifiers that themselves carry personal or commercially sensitive data may be masked in exported path evidence and impact reports while hop count, weakest-edge strength, termination reason and severity remain readable.
Break-glass reads during incident handling are permitted only with a recorded justification reference and an approving role, and are reported to the referenced audit model.

Historical membership lookups needed to answer a regulatory or legal request may cross retention-restricted snapshots only on the authority of the retention and privacy models, with the grant recorded here as a reference.
audit_requirements: Every traversal run, snapshot registration, lineage record and integrity check stores a reference to an audit record identifier issued by the referenced audit model; that model owns capture, integrity, retention and replay of the trail, and the reference held here confers none of those.

Reads of path evidence or cluster snapshots that are cited as membership evidence downstream must record the reading agent reference and the policy or rule version, so that the citation can later be reconstructed exactly.

Access exceptions, masking decisions and break-glass reads record the granting authority and the justification reference; this model evaluates none of them and takes no enforcement action on a failure.
Disclosure of a restricted integrity finding records the disclosing role, the recipient reference and the exception clause relied on.

required_fields: Owner or maintainer and accountable authority
read_order: AGENTS.md first, to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any other action, including for MongoDB or MCP deployments where the storage and interface entries name the collection or server rather than a file layout
The Specification URL, to load the WM-XCT-036 boundary, the in-scope and out-of-scope lists and the boundary notes, so that target-owned concerns are not attempted locally

The Storage type URL, to learn how edges, path reports, cluster snapshots, lineage records and integrity reports are projected into the deployed store and how canonical forms and digests are computed there
The Interface URL, to learn the available read and registration operations, their entitlement scopes and the mandatory fields returned with every path and snapshot record

The Processes URL, to learn the traversal policy approval, snapshot registration, lineage and integrity escalation procedures and the named owning authorities for cluster calculation and representative selection

coverage.claim: This structure covers the graph, traversal and cluster-boundary surface of WM-XCT-036 with primary grounding for every structural node: alias graph node and edge structure and edge annotation; per-predicate strength, symmetry and transitivity profiles; declared traversal policy with depth, path and repeated-node bounds and termination reporting; path provenance with weakest-edge reporting; the non-materialisation rule and contradiction markers; registration of externally calculated equivalence clusters as immutable, reproducible derived views; canonical representatives carried as external policy references; split and merge lineage with retained aliases, historical member lookup and downstream impact reporting; and the recurring graph pathologies reported as severity-bearing results. Ownership of matching, reasoning, merge, representative selection, enforcement, audit capture and retention execution is placed outside the model in composition links and boundary notes. The claim is bounded: it is not a claim of conformance to OWL 2, SKOS, SSSOM or ISO 25964-2, only of alignment.

checklist.notes: Edge identity with canonical tuple and digest, node identity left with the endpoint's system of record, snapshot and report identity under a master-system-first priority, and historical member lookup by identifier and instant. Grounded in RDF 1.2 IRI denotation, SSSOM subject/object/predicate slots and PROV-O entity identity.

Append-only edges with retraction and supersession, immutable snapshots superseded by revision, closed-and-succeeded representative decisions, and split/merge lineage events. Grounded in PROV-O derivation and revision; the lifecycle of the endpoint records and of the calculation rules themselves is explicitly left to their owners.

The alias edge is itself the relationship; predicate strength, symmetry and transitivity profiles determine composability; not-same edges are first-class; retained aliases and cross-cluster edges are tracked across lineage events.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset throughout; event time separated from observation or ingestion time for edge assertion, cluster change and representative effectiveness; snapshot instant separated from registration instant; effective intervals as instant pairs with open ends meaning still in force.

PROV-O-aligned attribution and derivation on path records, snapshots and lineage; per-edge justification references carried from the asserting authority; input digests and rule versions pinning every derived view.

Every derived view names its owning authority and rule version; five roles are defined with disjoint write rights; matching, reasoning, merge, representative selection, audit and retention are each assigned to a named external owner in composition and boundary notes.

Integrity conditions expressed with focus reference, condition code and severity following the SHACL validation-report shape; reproducibility and digest checks on artefacts; explicit statement that the runtime evaluator and any enforcement belong to the referenced validation service.

Deny by default with per-scope entitlement at bundle, layer, finding and artefact level; four exceptions including visibility of blocking markers and masking of sensitive endpoint identifiers; authorisation decisions and enforcement explicitly owned by the access model.

No hard delete by default; tombstones carry record identifier, reason, authority, event time and observation time; retention classes and schedules are set and executed by the referenced retention and privacy models; erasure impact is reported here but never executed here; endpoint deletion is out of scope and surfaces only as a stale-member finding.

Alignments to OWL 2, SKOS, SSSOM, PROV-O, SHACL and ISO 25964-2 with no conformance claim; mandatory export fields (assertion status, policy or rule version, weakest-edge strength, markers); prefix map versioned with the graph; unknown markers treated as blocking.

Named policy versions fix allowed predicates, direction, maximum depth, maximum paths and time budget; repeated-node and duplicate-path handling follows SPARQL 1.1 connectivity matching; every run reports a termination reason and a non-exhaustive flag.

Not-same edges, SKOS S46 disjointness and scope conflicts raise markers that travel with the record and block summarisation as confirmed equivalence; resolution is assigned to the owning authority, not performed here.

Weakest-edge reporting is mandatory and aggregation above the weakest link is prohibited; per-edge confidence is reported individually with its source; cluster stability and single-edge dependency are reported measures.

Snapshots require rule identifier, rule version, parameter set, input digest and snapshot instant, plus a reproducibility status flag; unreproducible snapshots are non-citable. The regeneration check itself is run by the calculation owner, which is a dependency this model reports on rather than controls.

No consulted standard defines how a representative is chosen within a set of co-denoting identifiers; OWL 2 and RDF 1.2 leave co-denoting IRIs equal in standing. The model therefore records only the reference to an external decision (authority, rule, version, scope, interval). The selection rule vocabulary itself is unsupported by primary sources and is deliberately not modelled here.

Alias equivalence between identifiers has no intrinsic spatial extent. Where endpoints denote spatially located subjects, location belongs to the subject's own model; jurisdictional scope of a representative decision is handled as a scope descriptor, not as geometry.

Integrity digests, append-only records and audit references are specified, but signing of edges by their asserting authority, key management and trust anchoring for federated assertions are not modelled and no primary source for them was consulted in this work.

known_omissions: Signature and trust-anchor semantics for federated alias assertions: how a receiving Dimension verifies that an edge really was asserted by the named authority is not modelled, and no primary source was consulted for it.

The vocabulary of representative-selection rules (source-priority, recency, completeness, jurisdiction) is deliberately absent because no consulted standard defines it; only the reference to an external decision is carried.

Context-dependent or scoped identity — the position that two identifiers may be interchangeable for one purpose and not another — is acknowledged through the substitution-license element and referentially opaque contexts, but a full contextual-identity mechanism is not modelled and rests on secondary sources only.

The schema.org sameAs property is widely used with a much weaker, page-reference meaning that conflicts with owl:sameAs; this was not verified against a primary source in this work and is recorded as a likely additional conflict rather than an established one.

Concrete numeric defaults for maximum hop depth, path count and cluster review thresholds are left to the adopting Dimension; the consulted sources support the need for bounds but supply no normative values.

Probabilistic or fuzzy equivalence models, and any calculus for combining confidence values along a chain, are excluded by the weakest-edge policy; alternatives exist in the literature and are not evaluated here.
Streaming or incremental cluster maintenance is not modelled; only whole-snapshot registration and revision are covered, which may not suit very high-churn graphs.
Cross-Dimension federation of the graph itself — how two adopting Dimensions exchange and reconcile their edge registers and policy profiles — is not modelled.
conflicts: SKOS makes skos:exactMatch transitive (S45) while explicitly refusing transitivity to skos:closeMatch to avoid compound errors across schemes; a single traversal cannot treat these predicates alike, so the composition table must be predicate-specific and closeMatch chains must be blocked rather than merely flagged.

OWL 2 SameIndividual asserts full interchangeability, which is stronger than most published alias data actually warrants; Halpin and colleagues argue it is often too strong and that referentially opaque contexts exist. The model resolves this by graded strength classes and explicit substitution licensing, at the cost of not being directly OWL-conformant.

SSSOM carries a numeric confidence per mapping, while OWL 2 identity is boolean and admits no degrees. Registering an SSSOM mapping as an alias edge therefore preserves confidence as reported evidence and never lets it be read as a partial owl:sameAs.

The absence of an alias edge means nothing under OWL 2's lack of a unique name assumption, whereas practical systems often read absence as difference. The model forbids reporting absence of a path as a difference claim, which will disappoint consumers expecting a closed-world answer.

RDF 1.2 Concepts is a Candidate Recommendation, not a Recommendation, at the time of writing; the triple-term and rdf:reifies mechanism used to justify edge-level annotation may still change, so the alignment is provisional.

ISO 25964-2's exact/inexact/partial equivalence distinctions and SKOS's closeMatch/exactMatch pair are related but not formally reconciled by either source; the mapping between the two lattices is an assumption of this model, and incomparable pairs must be declared rather than silently ordered.
regional_assumptions: Retention periods, lawful-basis requirements and erasure obligations for records that link personal identifiers vary by jurisdiction; the model carries a retention class reference and an impact report but assumes the adopting Dimension's retention and privacy models supply the jurisdiction-specific schedule and execute it.

The scope descriptor on a representative decision is expected to carry jurisdictional scope where a regulator mandates a particular identifier for a particular territory; the model permits concurrent scope-specific representatives rather than assuming one global canonical identifier.

Sources consulted are English-language W3C, IETF, ISO/NISO and open scientific material; sector- or nation-specific identity-equivalence rules (for example national registry crosswalk mandates) were not surveyed and may impose stricter constraints.

The assumption that endpoint identifiers are IRIs or otherwise globally scoped holds for linked-data and registry federations; deployments federating opaque local keys must first bind them to a governed namespace via the parent model before this mixin applies.
adversarial_checks: Attempted to justify owning cluster calculation locally, since the model already holds the edges and could compute connected components cheaply. Rejected: transitive closure over identity edges is an entailment computation whose correctness depends on predicate semantics owned elsewhere, and owning it would import reasoning lifecycle into a mixin. Reduced to registration, digesting and reproducibility checking of an externally supplied result.

Attempted to add a representative-selection rule set (source priority, recency, completeness). Rejected: no consulted standard supports any selection criterion, and modelling one would convert a preference decision into apparent equivalence semantics. Retained only the reference to the deciding authority, its rule version, scope and interval, and recorded the absence as a checklist gap.

Attempted to let the traversal function write a derived alias edge when a path of exactMatch edges is found, since exactMatch is transitive under SKOS S45. Rejected: transitivity licenses an inference, not a write, and materialising it would make this model the source of assertions it cannot justify. The non-materialisation rule and the assertion-status field were made mandatory on every derived record instead.

Tested whether an integrity check report constitutes enforcement or audit ownership. Concluded it does not: results carry focus, condition and severity and trigger nothing, the evaluator is referenced rather than owned, and audit capture is delegated. Wording in the finding, the function effects and the composition link was tightened so that no repair, retraction or notification-and-remediation is implied.

Tested whether a confidence value could safely be aggregated along a path to give a single score, which consumers repeatedly request. Rejected on the evidence that compound error across chained mappings is exactly what SKOS's non-transitive closeMatch guards against; weakest-edge reporting was made mandatory and aggregation above the weakest link prohibited.

Checked whether 'stale member' and 'orphaned representative' handling smuggles in endpoint lifecycle ownership. It does not: the model detects and annotates, referencing the upstream withdrawal record, and explicitly states that endpoint removal is executed by the master-data model and that immutable snapshots are annotated rather than edited.

Checked every artefact against the exclusive-representation rule and every finding for double representation. Five findings carry artefacts with a null rationale; four are inline-only with substantive rationales explaining why a published document would create a competing statement of edge existence, predicate profile, blocking marker or representative decision.

Re-read every bundle, layer, finding and function against each composition rationale looking for target-owned concepts. Moved reasoning closure, matching, merge, representative selection, authorisation decisions, audit capture and disposition execution out of the structural nodes and into composition links, out_of_scope entries and boundary notes.
